meta.title: FORGE — Special Forces / Military Operator Strength, Conditioning & Load-Carriage Library

Selection Candidate.training_age: 0-6 months structured lifting / pre-selection prep window 3-9 months out
Selection Candidate.ruck_pace: Build to 15:00/mile on flat terrain, no time pressure yet
Selection Candidate.work_capacity: Zone 2 aerobic base + basic circuit work, 50-60% effort, full recovery between hard efforts
Selection Candidate.grip_carry: Submaximal dead hangs and carries — build tendon/connective-tissue tolerance, no max holds
Selection Candidate.notes: Goal is bulletproofing the body for the volume ahead: own squat/hinge/press/pull/carry patterns, build an aerobic base, and get the ankles/knees/shoulders/feet used to load before intensity or ruck-pace pressure is added. This is injury-prevention season, not performance season.

Novice Operator.training_age: Post-selection, 0-12 months in a line unit / team
Novice Operator.work_capacity: Interval work 60-70% effort, structured work:rest ratios, kit-on conditioning introduced
Novice Operator.grip_carry: Working loads for farmer/suitcase carry, weighted hangs, first max-effort grip testing
Novice Operator.notes: Build general strength and work capacity onto the base while learning to train around an operational schedule — sessions need to survive being cut short or moved.

Intermediate Operator.training_age: 1-3 years operational, has been through at least one deployment cycle or equivalent workup
Intermediate Operator.work_capacity: Mixed-modal conditioning (sandbag/sled/bike/row), 70-80% effort, kit-on work standard
Intermediate Operator.grip_carry: Heavy carries at bodyweight-plus, max hang testing 1x/month, loaded rope climbs
Intermediate Operator.notes: This is the performance-building phase — strength, power, and load-bearing endurance all progress together, periodized around known training/deployment windows.

Advanced Operator.work_capacity: High-intensity mixed-modal blocks, 80%+ effort, fatigue-resistance under load is the target quality
Advanced Operator.grip_carry: Max-effort carries and hangs programmed deliberately, not just tested
Advanced Operator.notes: Training is individualized around accumulated wear and tear — durability and recoverability now matter as much as raw output. Autoregulate hard days against sleep/joint status.

Elite / Tier 1.intensity_power: Heavy load or max velocity, near-max intent
Elite / Tier 1.ruck_load: 65+ lb (30+ kg), mission/METL-driven rather than fixed
Elite / Tier 1.work_capacity: Programmed around actual mission tempo — maintenance-dose strength/power, conditioning follows the training cycle, not the other way around
Elite / Tier 1.grip_carry: Maintenance-level, tested rarely, trained only enough to hold the standard
Elite / Tier 1.notes: At this stage the program's job is to preserve output and joint health across a long career, not to chase new PRs. Minimum effective dose, ruthless prioritization, real recovery.

global_rules: Session order every day: explosive/power work first -> main strength lift -> posterior-chain/grip/carry -> conditioning only on a day NOT preceded by a heavy strength or ruck session.
Ruck load and pace progress independently of barbell load — never chase a ruck PR and a squat PR in the same week during Selection Candidate / Novice Operator phases.

All water-based training (swim conditioning, breath-hold, underwater work) is supervised, buddy-paired, and coached by a qualified water-safety/combat-diver instructor. This library gives programming structure only — it is never a substitute for in-water supervision, and no fixed breath-hold tables are prescribed here.
Heavy squat/hinge/pull days are placed 48h+ from a long ruck, a full work-capacity test, or a contact/CQB training day wherever the weekly schedule allows.
Grip and carry work is programmed, not just tested — max-effort dead hangs/carries are capped in frequency (see level_rules) to protect the elbows and lower back.
Any session can be compressed to its first two exercises if time or the operational schedule cuts it short — the order in this library is priority order, not just sequence.
This is a physical-preparation (S&C) library only: strength, conditioning, load carriage, and durability programming. It does not cover tactics, marksmanship, or any operational/skills training.
